paper.title: Generation from Noisy Examples
paper.summary: Studies adversarially noisy positive-example generation. The registered surface records the qualitative characterizations and separations, the unformalized numerical noisy-closure and sample-complexity frontier, and the source conflict over Definition D.1's trigger statistic.

formalization_scope.summary: Of sixteen cross-edition claim groups, twelve numbered qualitative results have full Lean coverage, numerical Definition 3.2 has partial proposition-level coverage, and three claims have no source-claim coverage: the quantitative Theorem 3.3 sample-complexity assertion, the proof-level Lemma 3.8 bound, and internally inconsistent Definition D.1 prose. The last claim has a non-covering correction link and is not a proof target.
specializations: Theorems 3.1 and 3.10 add an infinite ambient example type, while Theorem 3.3, Corollaries 3.4 and 3.7, Lemma 3.6, and Theorem C.3 add a nonempty example type; these assumptions repair false empty-class or empty-universe readings.
Lemmas 3.5 and D.2 use the concrete countably infinite universes constructed in their proofs rather than the false literal reading over every countable, possibly finite, universe.

Occurrence-level stream noise is converted only one way to distinct-value disagreement in noisy closure; exact-cardinality triggers can be vacuous on streams that never reach their thresholds, in both source and Lean.
The formal generators are semantic and noncomputable. No runtime, convergence-rate, membership-oracle, or effective-representation theorem is asserted.
Theorem 3.9 uses a totalized exact-half suffix and arbitrary fresh-candidate selection rather than reproducing Algorithm 1 extensionally; the theorem-level implication is preserved.

Lean follows the displayed Definition D.1 and Lemma D.2 proof, which count distinct positive observations, rather than the conflicting page-11 sentence claiming that D.1 counts all distinct observations.
gaps: No numerical extended-natural object NC_n(H), largest-witness value, or generic finite/infinite complement theorem is formalized.
The lower bound, Appendix-E upper threshold, and Theta(NC_n(H)) sample-complexity assertions following Theorem 3.3 are not formalized as numerical claims.
Lemma 3.8's proof-level quantitative assertion NC_n(H_i) < i is represented only by qualitative finiteness.

The page-11 Definition D.1 prose is internally inconsistent with the displayed definition and proof; it is registered as disputed and not planned, with the positive-count Lean definition linked only as a correction.

claims.title: Uniform noise-independent generation is characterized by the common intersection
claims.statement_summary: A countable UUS language class is uniformly generatable under arbitrary finite occurrence noise with a noise-independent distinct-observation threshold if and only if the intersection of all target supports is infinite.

source_assessment.notes: The printed statement is false for the empty class over a finite nonempty universe: generation is vacuous but the universal common intersection is finite. Lean adds an infinite ambient universe, automatic for every nonempty UUS class.

formalization.notes: The canonical wrapper records the intended nondegenerate equivalence with the necessary universe repair.

lean_links.notes: Infinite alpha excludes only the false empty-class finite-universe reading.

audit_refs.scope: Level 1 human statement correspondence only at checkpoint a66d3d0.
Pinned-arXiv statement audit of the equivalence and its universe repair.
Generated existence, module, and axiom audit for the wrapper.

claims.title: The n-noisy closure dimension records the largest finite-core witness size
claims.statement_summary: At noise level n, NC_n(H) is the largest number of distinct observations whose nonbottom noisy closure is finite, with value infinity for arbitrarily large witnesses and zero when no size-one witness exists.

source_assessment.notes: The distinct-sequence witness semantics are coherent. Source correctness is separate from Lean's deliberate proposition-level rather than numerical representation.

formalization.notes: Lean exactly represents witness semantics and qualitative finite boundedness, but does not define one extended-natural NC_n value or prove a generic finite/infinite complement law.

components.summary: A size-d witness is equivalently a finset or an injective sequence of d distinct examples with nonempty noisy version space and finite noisy common core.
NC_n(H) is finite exactly when sufficiently large samples with nonempty noisy version space have infinite noisy common core.
One extended-natural value records the largest witness size, zero and infinity cases, and a generic finite/infinite dichotomy.

lean_links.notes: Certifies the distinct-sequence witness semantics but creates no numerical dimension.
Exact qualitative finite side; no least numerical bound is selected.

audit_refs.scope: Pinned-arXiv audit of witness semantics, boundedness, and the missing numerical object; no human Definition 3.2 audit is claimed.

claims.title: Uniform noise-dependent generation is characterized by finite noisy closure dimension at every level
claims.statement_summary: A countable UUS language class has one generator with a threshold depending only on the occurrence-noise budget if and only if its noisy closure witnesses are bounded at every fixed noise level.

source_assessment.notes: The qualitative iff needs an inhabited example type: over the empty type and empty class, every dimension predicate is finite but no total generator exists. Quantitative prose is registered separately.

formalization.notes: Full coverage is for the qualitative theorem; numerical sample complexity is a separate card.

lean_links.notes: Nonempty alpha is an explicit source repair.

relations.notes: The right side is the qualitative finite part of Definition 3.2.

claims.title: Noisy closure dimension controls optimal uniform noisy-generation sample complexity
claims.statement_summary: At fixed noise level n, NC_n(H)=d gives a lower bound of d distinct observations, the Appendix-E strategy succeeds after max{NC_n(H)+1,n}, and the source summarizes sample complexity as Theta(NC_n(H)).

source_refs.notes: Uses max{NC_n(H)+1,n}, refining the main-text NC_n(H)+1 wording.
Uses max{NC_n(H)+1,n}, refining the main-text NC_n(H)+1 wording.

source_assessment.notes: Lean adds a nonempty example type so a generator is total in the empty-class edge case. The source proof's linear witness-cardinality estimate remains below this minimal canonical surface.

formalization.notes: The qualitative finite-class conclusion is complete under the inhabited-universe repair.

claims.title: Ordinary closure dimension zero can coexist with infinite one-noisy closure dimension
claims.statement_summary: There exists a countable UUS language class on a countably infinite universe whose ordinary closure dimension is zero but which has a finite-core one-noisy witness at every cardinality.

source_assessment.notes: The wording can be misread as an assertion on every countable X, false for finite X. The proof chooses a specific prime/power universe; Lean uses an incidence-isomorphic tagged countably infinite universe.

formalization.notes: Lean proves both dimension properties on a concrete universe matching the source proof's incidence structure.

lean_links.notes: The fixed universe is the intended existential witness, not an arbitrary finite countable universe.

relations.notes: Ordinary finite closure dimension does not imply noisy finite dimension.

claims.title: A diagonal finite-noisy-dimension cover suffices for nonuniform noisy generation
claims.statement_summary: If a UUS class is the union of one nondecreasing sequence H_i and H_i has finite noisy closure dimension at its matching level i, then the class is nonuniformly noise-dependent generatable.

source_assessment.notes: Lean adds a nonempty example type. It preserves the single fixed cover and diagonal condition, chosen before the unknown target and true noise level.

formalization.notes: The exact diagonal quantifier structure is preserved under the inhabited-universe repair.

source_assessment.notes: Lean adds a nonempty example type and handles finite or empty countable classes without requiring the source's informal infinite enumeration.

source_assessment.notes: The order is forall n, exists cover_n; it is intentionally weaker than the single diagonal cover in Lemma 3.6. The proof's numerical bound is registered separately.

claims.title: Alternate uniform noise-independent generation is characterized by bounded noisy-closure-dimension excess
